newsitem.title: FRANCE: BIS sells last CFC assets.
newsitem.headline: BIS sells last CFC assets.

text.p: French temporary work agency BIS is selling the remaining assets in bank CFC before the 1996 year end, a spokeswoman for the group said.
"Normally, the last assets will be sold before the end of the month," said Eve Magnant of the Publicis public relations agency. She could not give the value of the portfolio.

The impact of the sale of the assets is expected to be negative. This, together with an expected drop in 1996 results, explained the difference between the 490 franc price offered by Vendex International and the 533 franc share price of BIS when it was suspended on December 23, Magnant said.
A financial analyst said that the impact of the sale of loss-making CFC, which lends money to hotels and restaurants, would be a negative 230 million francs.
BIS earlier sold its security division HIFI to Adecco's Proteg in September.
BIS has 2,100 staff in France and Switzerland.
